items.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explains why he asked 60K employees to quit
items.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained why he offered buyouts to 60,000 of his employees in October, essentially urging them to voluntarily quit, rather than reducing the workforce via another massive layoff. The short answer is AI, but not in the way you might expect.

items.title: Microsoft CEO Nadella faces uncomfortable reality after outage
items.summary: Nadella’s comments come after disruptions hit Microsoft’s services and other major companies, putting digital infrastructure reliability back in focus.

items.title: Akamai Technologies (AKAM) Expands Mobile Enterprise Browser Security
items.summary: Akamai Technologies (NasdaqGS:AKAM) announced a new collaboration with Microsoft to secure Microsoft Edge for Business on mobile devices. The partnership targets iOS and Android, bringing enterprise browser controls such as real time threat prevention directly into Microsoft Edge for Business. Akamai says the integration also introduces generative AI governance features designed for corporate use of Microsoft Edge for Business on phones and tablets. items.title: Tech takes a beating as AI trade comes unstuck despite Anthropic surge
items.summary: Tech firms led losses across Asia once again Friday as Anthropic's sparkling debut failed to muster a recovery in sentiment towards the AI trade, with nerves frayed by worries over crisis-hit Nvidia, profitability and regulation."Whether Anthropic's IPO proves to be a defining moment for the AI trade remains to be seen.

items.title: How High Can ANT Stock Go? Wall Street Debut Sparks Valuation Debate – One Analyst Sees Amazon-Google Scale Opportunity In Anthropic
items.summary: William Blair called the IPO valuation “very reasonable” and said a higher sales multiple could put shares at $130 to $150.

items.title: Nvidia Backed AI Data Center Demand Puts Schneider Electric Stock In Focus
items.summary: AI returned to center stage when Anthropic’s IPO created about $81.3b in equity value and attracted heavyweight backers such as Nvidia, Google, Amazon, and Microsoft. That level of capital directed toward compute and power can draw attention to the less flashy picks and shovels behind the AI boom. items.title: Is Your VOO Fund Secretly An AI Bet?
items.summary: Most people treat an S&P 500 index fund as the safe default. The AI sell-off reads like a tech-stock story that index owners can watch from the side. The fund's own holdings say otherwise. About one dollar in four in the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO) sits in six AI giants.

items.title: IBM (IBM) Stock May Be 27% Below Fair Value On Quantum Platform News
items.summary: International Business Machines has pulled back sharply in recent months after a powerful multi year run, which puts a fresh spotlight on whether the current share price fairly reflects the cash that IBM can generate over time. Over the past 5 years the stock has returned 130.8%, so a lot of investor wealth now rests on how durable IBM's future cash flows prove to be.
